item.title: A recursion relation for the coefficients of Swinnerton-Dyer type polynomials
item.description: arXiv:2611.10034v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study a family of polynomials that are very closely related to the Swinnerton-Dyer polynomials. As main result, we determine a recursion relation for the coefficients of this family of polynomials. We briefly explain our own and others' interest in this family of polynomials.
item.dc:creator: Miek Messerschmidt

item.title: A singular homeomorphism between Pierce expansions and continued fraction expansions
item.description: arXiv:2611.10081v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we study the map $\Theta$ which sends each $x\in[0,1]$ to the number whose continued fraction digits are the first Pierce expansion digit of $x$ and the gaps between two consecutive Pierce expansion digits of $x$. We investigate the regularity of $\Theta$ and $\Theta^{-1}$, including the optimal H\"older exponent of $\Theta^{-1}$, and the local and Hausdorff dimensions of the push-forwards of the Lebesgue measure under $\Theta$ and $\Theta^{-1}$. We also study the differentiability of $\Theta$ at rational and irrational points, and calculate the Hausdorff dimension of the set of points at which $\Theta$ has an infinite derivative.
item.dc:creator: Min Woong Ahn

item.title: An elliptic deformation of continued fractions
item.description: arXiv:2611.10104v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We construct an elliptic deformation $\mathcal{Q}_{a,b;q,p}(x)$ of positive rational numbers $x$ by attaching Schlosser's small elliptic weights $w_{a,b;q,p}(s,t)$ to prefixes of Stern--Brocot words. On positive integers $n$ it gives Schlosser's elliptic numbers $[n]_{a,b;q,p}$. Parameter shifts realize $x \mapsto x+1$ and $x \mapsto x/(x+1)$, while a reciprocal parameter transformation gives an inversion formula. The Gaussian degeneration recovers the $q$-deformed rationals of Morier-Genoud and Ovsienko. The regular and negative elliptic continued fractions agree, since they evaluate the same word with the same ordered weights. The numerator and denominator satisfy weighted Farey recursions and, for rationals greater than $1$, are the closure polynomials, or quiver $F$-polynomials, of the associated oriented type-$A$ quivers. Finally, we express the vertex weights as normalized elliptic Euler expressions of balanced virtual torus representations.
item.dc:creator: Shintarou Yanagida

item.title: Motivic generating functions and $L$-derivatives of cohomological automorphic representations
item.description: arXiv:2611.10478v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Forty years ago, Gross and Zagier proved a remarkable formula computing the central derivative of the Rankin--Selberg $L$-function of a cusp form $f$ of weight $2$ and a character of the class group of an imaginary quadratic field, satisfying the so-called Heegner condition, and deduce that the nonvanishing of the central derivative implies the nonvanishing of the corresponding Mordell--Weil rank. This formula was later generalized in various contexts and degrees, for example, by S. Zhang for $f$ of higher even weights; and by Yuan--Zhang--Zhang for $f$ a Hilbert cusp form of parallel weight $2$ over an arbitrary totally real field $F$ and $\chi$ a Dirichlet character of an arbitrary CM extension $E/F$, allowing arbitrary ramification. In this article, we prove a Gross--Zagier type formula in the context of doubling method, for $f$ a Hilbert cusp form over $F$ and $\chi$ a Hecke character of $E$ of general weights under a balancing condition, again allowing arbitrary ramification. Indeed, we even formulate a general conjecture which we call the motivic arithmetic inner product formula, for cohomological automorphic representations of $\mathrm{GL}_{2r}$ over $E$ of hermitian type of balanced weights.
item.dc:creator: Yifeng Liu

item.title: Local vanishing density of order $1$ and Divisor moments
item.description: arXiv:2611.10489v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We establish a general framework relating local vanishing densities of order $1$ to logarithmic growth of divisor moments on regular arithmetic curves. As applications, we recover classical divisor moment estimates for polynomial values and establish their function field analogue. Furthermore, under GRH, we obtain a result on divisor moments for polynomials in the Fourier coefficients of non-CM cuspidal eigenforms with trivial nebentypus and trivial inner twist. The Fourier coefficients need not be integers, and the polynomials need not be squarefree. Under additional analytic hypotheses, we also allow a Sato--Tate angle restriction.
item.dc:creator: Wonwoong Lee

item.title: Multivariate Pellarin $L$-values on algebraic curves
item.description: arXiv:2611.10495v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We establish a generating trace formula for multicharacter ideal-type $L$-values associated with rank-one Drinfeld modules. For a sign-normalized Hayes module with free period lattice, the formula realizes the $L$-values at weights $n\equiv s\pmod{q^{\deg_\infty}-1}$ as a trace over the ordinary Hilbert class field. We further characterize the polynomials in the exponential variable $X$ arising in multicharacter lattice generating identities over arbitrary function rings. Their coefficients are given explicitly via the shtuka basis, which gives concrete control over their supports and degrees. This completely settles an open problem of Pellarin and Perkins: these polynomials are all constant if and only if $s<2q$. The results on coefficients apply to curves of arbitrary genus, infinite places of arbitrary degree, and nonprincipal period lattices.
item.dc:creator: Chuangqiang Hu, Stephen S. -T. Yau, Lishan Yu

item.title: A Goldbach-Type Problem for the Unitary M\"obius Function
item.description: arXiv:2611.10499v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $g(n)=(-1)^{\omega(n)}$, where $\omega(n)$ denotes the number of distinct prime factors of $n$. We prove that, for every sufficiently large integer $N$, each ordered additive sign pattern $(g(a),g(N-a))=(s,t)$ occurs at least $N/(128(\log N)^3)$ times. We also prove that, for every $N\ge18$ and every $s,t\in\sgnset$, there is at least one integer $1\le a<N$ such that $(g(a),g(N-a))=(s,t)$. In addition, we establish a one-quarter asymptotic formula for almost all target integers. Finally, we discuss Goldbach-type problems for the ordinary M\"obius function and formulate related questions.
item.dc:creator: Tian Caolin, Yang Chenxi

item.title: On the error term in Gauss's mean value formulas for class numbers
item.description: arXiv:2611.10606v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Combining the frameworks of Chamizo--Iwaniec and Chamizo--Ubis with the recent character-sum and exponential-sum estimates of Bellotti and Kerr, we improve the error term in Gauss's mean value formulas for class numbers of binary quadratic forms from $O(N^{21/32+\eps})$ to $O(N^{55/84+\eps})$. If no Dirichlet $L$-function vanishes in $\mathrm{Re}\,s>7/8$, the exponent becomes $2274811/3487744$; under the Generalized Riemann Hypothesis for quadratic Dirichlet $L$-functions, it becomes $118/181$.
item.dc:creator: Bingxin Jia, Caihua Luo, Xu Song, Wei Xiong

item.title: Trivial solutions in Generalized Fermat equations
item.description: arXiv:2611.10667v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The modular method is a powerful tool to study generalized Fermat equations. Trivial solutions often become an obstruction to the method. While using hypergeometric motives to construct Galois representations, some of these solutions give rise to newforms with complex multiplication. In the present article, assuming a standard conjecture in Darmon's program, we prove that asymptotically any newform with complex multiplication cannot be related to a non-trivial primitive solution. This allows to discard all such newforms, including those associated to trivial solutions.
item.dc:creator: Pedro-Jos\'e Cazorla Garc\'ia, Ariel Pacetti, Lucas Villagra-Torcomian

item.title: Restricted Quantum unique ergodicity under Generalized Lindel\"of conjecture
item.description: arXiv:2611.10676v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Assume the generalized Lindel\"of hypothesis. Let $u$ be an even Hecke--Maass cusp form on $\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{Z})\backslash\mathbb{H}$, normalized in $L^2$ with respect to hyperbolic area, with Laplace eigenvalue $1/4+T^2$. For every fixed $\psi\in C_c((0,\infty);\mathbb{C})$ and every $\varepsilon>0$, we prove that \[ \int_0^\infty \psi(y)|u(i y)|^2\frac{d y}{y} =\frac{6}{\pi}\int_0^\infty \psi(y)\frac{d y}{y} +O_{\psi,\varepsilon}(T^{-1/4+\varepsilon}) \] as $T\to\infty$, uniformly in $u$. In particular, the restriction mass equidistributes on every fixed compact segment of the imaginary axis in $\mathbb{H}$.
item.dc:creator: Qingfeng Sun, Qizhi Zhang

item.title: A quantitative two-interval criterion for the Riemann hypothesis
item.description: arXiv:2611.10726v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We aim to study whether the Weil form can detect a zero of the Riemann zeta function away from the critical line using two functions with increasingly narrow, widely separated supports. We prove that the Riemann hypothesis is equivalent to the Cauchy-Schwarz inequality on every such pair at all sufficiently large separations, provided the component widths decrease subexponentially. A zero to the right of the critical line forces the normalized cross term to exceed an exponential at arbitrarily large separations, with any exponent smaller than the horizontal displacement of that zero. In particular, reciprocal-width intervals suffice. Our proof combines a short-support positivity estimate, a smooth partition of fixed test functions and a pole obstruction for a one-sided Laplace transform. We also express the cross term through prime powers in a moving multiplicative interval. The resulting criterion specifies a uniform arithmetic inequality whose proof would establish the Riemann hypothesis.
item.dc:creator: Payam Danesh

item.title: On the lower bound for the $L^1$ norm of Liouville exponential sums. II
item.description: arXiv:2611.10790v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $\lambda$ denote the Liouville function, and put \[ I_\lambda(X)=\int_0^1\left|\sum_{n\le X}\lambda(n)e^{2\pi i n\alpha}\right|\,d\alpha. \] In this paper, we prove that \[ \limsup_{X \to \infty} \frac{\log I_{\lambda}(X)}{\log X} \ge \frac{1}{3}. \]
item.dc:creator: Ben Krause, Jiangpeng Li, Yu-Chen Sun, Hui Wang

item.title: New lower bounds for even and odd values of the partition function
item.description: arXiv:2611.10899v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $N_{\mathrm{odd}}(X)$ and $N_{\mathrm{even}}(X)$ denote the numbers of integers $0\leq n< X$ for which the ordinary partition function $p(n)$ is odd and even, respectively. The Parkin--Shanks conjecture predicts that $N_{\mathrm{odd}}(X)$ and $N_{\mathrm{even}}(X)$ are both asymptotic to $X/2$. Bella\"iche and Nicolas proved that $N_{\mathrm{even}}(X)\gg \sqrt{X} \log \log X$, while Zheng, building on work of Ono and Swaminathan, recently proved that $N_{\mathrm{odd}}(X)\gg \sqrt{X}$. We improve both bounds simultaneously by proving $\min\{N_{\mathrm{odd}}(X), N_{\mathrm{even}}(X)\}\gg X^{3/4}/(\log X \log \log X)$.
item.dc:creator: Liuquan Wang

item.title: Diophantine definitions of nonsplitting for central simple algebras over global fields
item.description: arXiv:2611.10924v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For every global field and every fixed degree, we prove that the structure constants defining nonsplit central simple algebras form a diophantine set. We formulate a local witness principle separating reliable localization, exact localization, and local detection. Adapted Kummer and Artin--Schreier presentations provide a common construction of witnesses through a uniform radical formula and ramification matching. This gives an independent proof of the non-characteristic case, which also follows from Morrison's nonnorm theorem, and treats the characteristic-degree case by the same method. We recover prime-degree nonnorm definability and give applications to rootless polynomials, anisotropic quadratic forms in all characteristics, and generalized Severi--Brauer varieties.
item.dc:creator: Guang Hu

item.title: On mod p Hecke algebras of abstract p-adic automorphic forms
item.description: arXiv:2611.11142v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study completed local shallow Hecke algebras acting on residual automorphic forms attached to projective augmented modules for $\GL_2(\Q_p)$. For odd primes $p$, we prove that the maximal ideal has nilpotence exponent $O(p^{r/2})$ on the level-$r$ generalized eigenspace. For $p\ge5$, if the corresponding Hecke eigenspace in the residual smooth dual has finite length as a $\GL_2(\Q_p)$-representation, then the completed local algebra is noetherian of Krull dimension at least two. If, in addition, its cotangent space has dimension at most two, then it is a formal power series ring in two variables. The nilpotence bound follows by conjugating level subgroups. To deduce the dimension bound, we replace the Fourier pairing in the classical nilpotence method with an inequality comparing the dimension of each finite-level generalized eigenspace with that of its Hecke eigenspace. We apply these results to modular curves and definite quaternion algebras.
item.dc:creator: Nha Xuan Truong

item.title: On Rankin Invariants of Ideal Lattices
item.description: arXiv:2611.11190v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Rankin constant $\gamma_{n,k}$ measures the largest discriminant of a densest rank $k$ sublattice of a lattice in $\R^n$ over all such lattices of rank $n$ and their exact values are mostly open. For a general lattice $L\subset \R^n$ of rank $n$, the problem of determining its Rankin invariant $\gamma_{n,k}(L)$ is to find the discriminant of such a densest sublattice. There are no general formulas to compute the discriminant of any arbitrary rank $k$ sublattice. This paper specializes to the case of ideal lattices arising from ideals of number fields, and provides two approaches to study Rankin constants: first, we propose a systematic approach to approximate the minimum discriminant by introducing subideal lattices and proving a closed-form formula to compute $\gamma^{ideal}_{n,k}(L)$, the ideal Rankin invariant of the ideal lattice. Subsequently, we establish necessary conditions on the underlying number field for the existence of an ideal lattice admitting an optimal subideal lattice with a prescribed minimum discriminant. Secondly, we consider ideal lattices with arbitrary sublattices. We compute $\gamma_{9,2}$ and improve the current known bounds of the Rankin constants $\gamma_{5,2}$, $\gamma_{7,2}$ and $\gamma_{9,3},\gamma_{9,4}$, and provide an algebraic construction of the lattice that was used in dimensions $5$ and $7$.
item.dc:creator: Yuan Xiang Chew, Fr\'ed\'erique Oggier

item.title: Statistics of centralizers of integer matrices
item.description: arXiv:2611.11287v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: With recent interests on the statistics of commuting integer matrices, we study the related problem on the statistics of the set of centralizer of a matrix. We provide asymptotics and bounds on the size of such set when restricted to integer matrices of bounded height.
item.dc:creator: Muhammad Afifurrahman, Wildan Bagus Wicaksono

item.title: New families of maximal curves not covered by the Hermitian curve and their cyclic automorphism groups
item.description: arXiv:2611.11298v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For every prime power $q>2$, integer $n\ge2$ and $1\le r\le 2n-1$, we construct an $\mathbb F_{q^{2n}}$-maximal curve $T_{q,n,r}$ with Kummer equation \[ z^{q^n+1}=\eta^{-R}y(1-y^{q-1})^R, \qquad \frac{q^r-1}{q-1},\] where $\eta\in\mathbb F_{q^{2n}}^*$ satisfies $\eta^{q^n}=-\eta$. For fixed $q,n$, these are cyclic covers of the projective line over a single field, indexed by the integer $r$. Writing $\delta=\gcd(q^n+1,R)$, we prove that the genus is $(q-1)(q^n+1-\delta)/2$ and that $T_{q,n,r}$ is covered by the Hermitian curve $\mathcal H_{q^n}$ over an algebraic closure if and only if $\min(r,2n-r)$ divides $n$. For $1<r<n$ and $\delta=1$, the full automorphism group is cyclic of order $(q-1)(q^n+1)$, and distinct values of $r$ give curves that are nonisomorphic over an algebraic closure despite having the same genus and full automorphism group. We also give explicit equations and genera for all their Galois subfields. When $n\ge 4$ is a power of two, this produces families over a fixed field whose members are not covered by $\mathcal H_{q^n}$.
item.dc:creator: Xubin Hu, Liming Ma, Yipeng Wang

item.title: On quantitative aspects of ideal membership certificate and GCD inequality for polynomials evaluated at almost units
item.description: arXiv:2611.11341v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we obtain an effective bounds for the ideal membership certificate in polynomial rings over almost all rings of S-integers, thereby generalizing results of Aschenbrenner and Evertse and Gyory. We also establish an effective refinement of a result of Xiao, building on earlier work of Levin and Corvaja and Zannier. In particular, we provide explicit bounds for both the number and the total degrees of the exceptional hypersurfaces arising in an inequality that bounds the greatest common divisor of multivariable polynomials evaluated at almost S-units under consideration. As an application of our results, we obtain an effective refinement of a theorem of Corvaja and Zannier: Let $(F_n)_n$ and $(G_n)_n$ be two linear recurrence sequences and $\mathcal{N}$ be the set of positive integers $n$ such that $F_n/G_n$ is an integer. Hadamard quotient theorem, conjectured by Pisot and proven by Van der Poorten states that if the set $\mathcal{N}$ coincides with $\mathbb{N}$ then $\left(F_n/G_n\right)_n$ is itself linear recurrence sequence. Corvaja-Zannier proved that if $\mathcal{N}$ is infinite set, then there exists a nonzero polynomial $P(X)$ such that $\left( P(n)F_n/G_n\right)_n$ agrees with a linear recurrence sequence for all $n$ in a suitable arithmetic progression. We give an explicit bound $C$, depending explicitly on the parameters of the recurrence sequences such that, the conclusion holds if $\mathcal{N}$ contains at least $C$ elements.
item.dc:creator: Armand Noubissie

item.title: Smooth approximations to character sums and zeta sums
item.description: arXiv:2611.11389v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study smooth approximations to Dirichlet character sums and zeta sums. The uniform upper-bound consequence of the Granville--Soundararajan conjecture, when imposed on all nonprincipal characters including imprimitive ones, implies the Riemann hypothesis for every primitive nonprincipal Dirichlet \(L\)-function. The proof uses characters induced to moduli divisible by all small primes. In the other direction, assuming the Riemann hypothesis for \(L(s,\chi)\), we establish the conjectured approximation uniformly for \(q^a\le x\le q\), where \(0<a\le1\) is fixed, with \(y=(\log q+(\log x)^2)(\log\log q)^C\) for every fixed \(C>6\). In this range both the character sum and its smooth restriction, and hence their difference, are exponentially small relative to the number of \(y\)-smooth integers coprime to \(q\). We establish the corresponding approximation for \(\sum_{n\le x}n^{-it}\) under the Riemann hypothesis for the zeta function, uniformly for \(T^a\le x\le T\) and \(2T\le t\le5T\). We also show that the full zeta-sum smooth-approximation conjecture implies the Lindel\"of hypothesis.
item.dc:creator: Zikang Dong, Shengbo Zhao, Guang-Liang Zhou

item.title: Revisiting the conjectures of Shapiro and Schanuel
item.description: arXiv:2611.11404v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We tackle Shapiro's conjecture for exponential polynomials where the coefficients are polynomials, and show that it follows from Schanuel's conjecture. More concretely, given exponential polynomials $f$ and $g$ with infinitely many common zeros, we show that Schanuel's conjecture implies that there is an exponential polynomial $h$ vanishing precisely at all the common zeros of $f$ and $g$.
item.dc:creator: Paola D'Aquino, Sebastian Eterovi\'c

item.title: 2-Selmer in arithmetic progressions
item.description: arXiv:2611.11413v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove uniform asymptotics for the 2-Selmer cardinality in the congruent number family $y^2=x^3-D^2x$ with twisting parameter $D$ restricted to long arithmetic progressions.
item.dc:creator: Giacomo Bortolussi

item.title: Monotonicity of Erd\H{o}s sums
item.description: arXiv:2611.11418v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For $k \geq 1$ let $f_k = \sum_{\Omega(n)=k} 1/(n\log n)$, where $\Omega$ counts prime factors with multiplicity, and let $g_k$ be the same sum restricted to odd $n$. Lichtman showed that $f_k \to 1$, with a global minimum at $k=6$, and Gorodetsky, Lichtman and Wong that $f_k = 1 - 2^{-k}(a_1 k^2 + O(k \log(k+1)))$. We prove that $f_k < f_{k+1}$ for every $k \geq 6$, and that $g_k > g_{k+1}$ for every $k \geq 1$. The two statements come from one analytic distinction. Writing $\sum_k P_k(s) z^k = \zeta(s)^z H(s,z)$, at $s=1$ the point $z=2$ lies on the first singular circle of $H$, and strictly inside the first singular circle of the product with the prime $2$ removed. We show that this distinction decides the direction in general. If the complement of a set of primes $\mathcal{P}$ is thin and its least element is at least $3$, the corresponding sums eventually decrease, so the second theorem is one case of a general phenomenon. The inequalities used at the last step of the first theorem are certified by interval arithmetic.
item.dc:creator: Jaideep Sai Padhi

item.title: Ranks of fibers in random elliptic surfaces
item.description: arXiv:2611.11432v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For random integer polynomials $P$ of arbitrary degree we prove that for $100\%$ of elliptic surfaces $y^2=x^3-P(t)^2x$ the average 2-Selmer rank of the fibers is 3. Consequently, for $100\%$ these random elliptic surfaces we establish a lower bound for the proportion of fibers attaining algebraic rank $0$ and $1$.
item.dc:creator: Giacomo Bortolussi

item.title: A rank-zero $2$-converse to the Gross--Zagier and Kolyvagin theorem for elliptic curves with abelian two-division field
item.description: arXiv:2611.11566v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $E/\mathbb{Q}$ be an elliptic curve with abelian two-division field. We prove that finiteness of ${\mathrm Sel}_{2^\infty}(E/\mathbb{Q})$ implies $L(E,1)\ne0$. The proof follows the quadratic twist deformation approach of OpenAI: Beilinson--Kato elements are interpolated over the cyclotomic $\mathbb{Z}_2$-extension and over families of quadratic twists, and congruences in the resulting group ring transfer non-vanishing from the twists to $E$. The integral control of this interpolation is governed by one cohomological $\mu$-invariant, which depends only on $E[2]$ and vanishes for abelian two-division fields. Together with Kato's cyclotomic divisibility and the fixed lattice in his construction, it bounds the denominator by a fixed power of $2$, independently of the twisting primes and the family dimension. Congruences among coefficients of a half-integral-weight form, in the style of Ono--Skinner, construct the required twist families.
item.dc:creator: Ashay Burungale, Ye Tian

item.title: On the $\Delta$-primitive squares conjecture
item.description: arXiv:2611.11574v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A natural number $n$ has the $\Delta$ property if some difference of complementary divisors of $n$ is the sum of two such differences; equivalently, if some split graph has a factor graph containing an $n$-simple triangle. In additive terms, $n$ has the $\Delta$ property exactly when the positive part of the factor-difference set of $n$, introduced by Erd\H{o}s and Rosenfeld, is not sum-free. The set $\mathbb{N}(\Delta)$ of such numbers is closed under multiplication by squares, and it was conjectured that it contains infinitely many $\Delta$-primitive perfect squares. We prove this conjecture, and show that these squares can be chosen to avoid any prescribed finite set of primes but $3$.
item.dc:creator: Franco Golfieri, Victor N. Schv\"ollner

item.title: $C_{\st}$-conjecture for compactly supported pro-\'etale cohomology
item.description: arXiv:2611.11589v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove the \'etale-de Rham direction of the $C_{\st}$-conjecture for compactly supported cohomology of smooth partially proper rigid analytic varieties over local fields of mixed characteristic. More precisely, we recover filtered de Rham cohomology and (under a finite-rank assumption) Hyodo--Kato cohomology from compactly supported $p$-adic pro-\'etale cohomology as derived Hom (in a category of Arithmetic Topological Vector Spaces) with values in $\B_{\pdr}$ and $\B_{\pFF}$ respectively (period rings related to $\B_{\dr}$ and $\B_{\st}$ whose higher Galois cohomology vanishes). The proof uses, via the geometrized basic comparison theorem, Poincar\'e duality for Hyodo--Kato and (filtered) de Rham cohomology, explicit extension calculations for period sheaves, and fully-faithfulness of the passage from Galois equivariant perfect complexes on the Fargues--Fontaine curve to Arithmetic Topological Vector Spaces.
item.dc:creator: Pierre Colmez, sally Gilles, Zhenghui Li, Wies{\l}awa Nizio{\l}

item.title: Simple algebraic groups with good reduction, the genus problem, and unramified cohomology
item.description: arXiv:2611.11631v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We obtain a number of new results on the arithmetic of linear algebraic groups over higher-dimensional fields. In particular, we resolve some key open questions over 2-dimensional global fields, such as the finiteness of the genus of spinor groups of quadratic forms of dimension $\geq 10$. We also extend various finiteness results to new classes of fields, including function fields of $p$-adic surfaces. Our arguments rely in a crucial way on new finiteness results for unramified cohomology.
item.dc:creator: Igor A. Rapinchuk

item.title: An Analytic Evaluation of Euler Sharp Sums
item.description: arXiv:2611.11972v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We give a direct analytic evaluation of the Euler sharp sums $\zeta^\sharp(2,\{1\}^{d-3},\overline{2})$ for all even integers $d\ge4$, expressing them in terms of ordinary multiple zeta values of depth at most two. The proof reduces these sharp sums to a harmonic-number series and evaluates it using a generating-function identity, thereby proving the even-depth case of a conjecture of Xu and Zhao.
item.dc:creator: Zhenlu Wang, Ce Xu, Jianqiang Zhao

item.title: Super-positivity via Dirichlet theta functions
item.description: arXiv:2611.12152v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $\chi$ be a quadratic Dirichlet character and let $\Lambda(\chi, s)$ be its associated completed $L$-function. The super-positivity property, introduced by Yun--Zhang (2017), asserts that $\Lambda^{(m)} \left( \frac{1}{2}, \chi \right) \geq 0$ for all $m \geq 0$. We show that a certain positivity property of its Dirichlet theta function $\theta(t, \chi)$, namely that $\theta(t, \chi)>0$ for all $t \geq 1$, implies the super-positivity property for $\chi$. We then investigate a refined form of the above property: we conjecture that the sequence $\{ \Lambda^{(2m)}\left(\frac{1}{2}, \chi \right )\}_{ m \geq 0}$ is always eventually increasing and has at most one turning point, and we prove these assertions again when $\theta(t, \chi)>0$ for $t \geq 1$.
item.dc:creator: Arshay Sheth, Wayne Voo

item.title: Linear disjointness and values of Mahler M-functions
item.description: arXiv:2611.12396v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that the algebra generated by the values of Mahler M-functions at algebraic points admits a decomposition as the tensor product, over Q, of a countable family of linearly disjoint algebras. Consequently, the study of linear and algebraic relations among such values reduces to the corresponding problem within each of these smaller algebras. Our proof relies on recent advances of the authors on Mahler's method in several variables. As an application, we obtain a complete description of the algebraic relations among the values of the Fredholm series and their derivatives at nonzero algebraic points. This fully resolves an old problem originating in Mahler's work.
item.dc:creator: Colin Faverjon (LAMFA,CNRS), Boris Adamczewski (CTN,CNRS,CIRM)

item.title: Nontrivial Zeros of the Riemann Zeta Function and Its Derivative
item.description: arXiv:2611.12438v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The nontrivial zeros of the Riemann zeta function lie at the heart of analytic number theory. Through the explicit formulas, they govern the distribution of prime numbers: the closer all nontrivial zeros lie to the critical line $\Re(s)=\frac12$, the more uniformly the primes are distributed. The Riemann Hypothesis-asserting that all nontrivial zeros satisfy $\Re(s)=\frac12$-is equivalent to the optimal error bound $O(\sqrt{x}\log x)$ in the Prime Number Theorem. Beyond number theory, the zeros of $\zeta(s)$ and its derivative $\zeta'(s)$ are deeply intertwined: the horizontal distribution of $\zeta'$-zeros near the critical line encodes information about the spacing of consecutive $\zeta$-zeros. This paper establishes some results concerning the nontrivial zeros of the Riemann zeta function.
item.dc:creator: Chuancun Yin, Xianghua Zhao, Zuolu Hao, Zhongyang Sun

item.title: An asymptotic formula for primes of the form $u^2+v^2+1$
item.description: arXiv:2611.12467v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove Motohashi's conjecture on primes of the form $u^2+v^2+1$, with Iwaniec's corrected constant. Let $b$ denote the characteristic function of the positive integers representable as a sum of two squares. Then, as $x\to\infty$, \[ \sum_{p\le x}b(p-1) =\kappa\Spr\frac{x}{(\log x)^{3/2}} +O\!\left(\frac{x}{(\log x)^{3/2}\sqrt{\log\log x}}\right), \] where $\kappa$ is the Landau--Ramanujan constant and $\Spr=\prod_{p\equiv3\,({\rm mod}\,4)}\bigl(1-1/(p(p-1))\bigr)$. The proof combines auxiliary prime factors with a mean square estimate for bilinear sums. We obtain the minor arc bound through harmonic switching and high moments, replacing arithmetic divisibility conditions by independent projective lines. We remove the auxiliary weights using Selberg's sieve.
item.dc:creator: Yujiao Jiang, Yuk-Kam Lau, Guangshi L\"u

item.title: Horizontal estimates for Kloosterman sums under Hecke eigenvalue constraints
item.description: arXiv:2611.12500v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove weighted cancellation under small-value conditions on Hecke eigenvalues of finitely many non-CM holomorphic newforms. We also obtain many squarefree integers of each sign with fixed normalized amplitude, simultaneously small Hecke eigenvalues, and a fixed bound on the number of prime factors, uniformly in growing reduced residue classes. Our questions are motivated by Xi's noncorrelation conjectures and the mixed-moment estimates of Jiang and Lau. Their estimates imply that small Hecke eigenvalues can occur together with non-small Kloosterman values. Our result retains this property with a fixed prime-factor bound, both signs, and the residue conditions. Using OpenAI's zero-free half-plane theorem for Dirichlet $L$-functions, we give an example with at most $83$ prime factors, normalized amplitude at least $10^{-21}$, and moduli $M\le C^{11/200}$.
item.dc:creator: Hongze Li, Mingxuan Zhong

item.title: Ternary quadratic genera and generalized Hurwitz class numbers via quaternion orders
item.description: arXiv:2611.12528v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We classify the genera of primitive positive definite ternary quadratic forms in the extremal cases of Lehman's level and discriminant conditions. The genera are parametrized by their level, discriminant, and genus conductor, which also distinguishes local forms having the same isotropy. Using the correspondence with quaternion orders of level $(N_1,N_2)$, we express their weighted representation numbers and class numbers in terms of generalized modified Hurwitz class numbers. The formulas allow arbitrary admissible prime power exponents and include the additional genera obtained by Watson's transformation. As an application, we determine all $255$ one-class genera in these families and give an explicit representation formula for each. Of these formulas, $110$ concern nonsquarefree $N_1N_2$.
item.dc:creator: Yifan Luo, Tianze Wang, Haigang Zhou

item.title: Independence of Hasse--Weil $L$-functions over rings of Dirichlet series
item.description: arXiv:2611.12541v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study linear and algebraic independence of Hasse--Weil $L$-functions of abelian varieties over $\mathbb{Q}$, with Dirichlet series as coefficients. For nonzero varieties that are pairwise non-isogenous over $\overline{\mathbb{Q}}$, we prove that their $L$-functions with arbitrary Dirichlet twists, together with all their derivatives and $1$, are linearly independent when the coefficient series use only primes from a set of natural density zero. For untwisted $L$-functions, this independence is equivalent to the condition that the varieties are pairwise non-isogenous over $\mathbb{Q}$. If the individual monodromy groups are connected, the result for varieties that are pairwise non-isogenous over $\overline{\mathbb{Q}}$ extends to larger coefficient rings: the prime supports of coefficients are unrestricted outside a prescribed set of positive upper natural density and meet it in a set of natural density zero. We also characterize algebraic independence of untwisted $L$-functions in terms of the multiplicities of the simple isogeny factors of the varieties. The proofs combine an arithmetic-function lemma of Kaczorowski--Molteni--Perelli with Frobenius density arguments and require no analytic continuation or automorphy.
item.dc:creator: Sho Yoshikawa

item.title: A relative trace formula for the orthogonal Gan-Gross-Prasad model and the proof of its fundamental lemma
item.description: arXiv:2611.12724v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we propose a comparison of relative trace formulas to study the Gan--Gross--Prasad conjecture. We unfold the relative trace formulas, match their regular orbits, and formulate the corresponding fundamental lemma and smooth transfer conjecture. Finally, we prove the fundamental lemma for the unit element of the Hecke algebra.
item.dc:creator: Zhengyu Mao, Chen Wan

item.title: On the higher-order Titchmarsh divisor problem
item.description: arXiv:2611.12756v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For every fixed integer $k\geq2$ and every fixed nonzero integer $h$, we prove that, as $x\to\infty$, \begin{equation*} \sum_{x<n\leq2x}\Lambda(n)\tau_k(n+h) \sim C_{k,h}x(\log x)^{k-1}, \end{equation*} where $\tau_k$ is the $k$-fold divisor function and $C_{k,h}>0$ is a constant depending only on $k$ and $h$.
item.dc:creator: Guangwei Hu, Guangshi L\"u, Zhiwei Wang, Jie Wu

item.title: Why the non-abelian Gyarmati--Matolcsi--Ruzsa inequality does not generally work: mechanisms and explicit examples
item.description: arXiv:2611.12776v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For finite sets in a commutative semigroup, Gyarmati, Matolcsi and Ruzsa proved \[ |A_1+\dots+A_n|^{n-1}\ \le\ \prod_{i=1}^n|A_1+\dots+A_{i-1}+A_{i+1}+\dots+A_n| . \] They asked whether in an arbitrary group \[ |A_1\cdots A_n|^{n-1}\ \le\ \prod_{i=1}^n\ \max_{a\in A_i}\,|A_1\cdots A_{i-1}\,a\,A_{i+1}\cdots A_n| , \] where each omitted set is replaced by the largest slice obtained by fixing one of its elements. Nair, Namayandeh and Zhu proved that this inequality does not hold when $n=4$ and $G=D_4^{14}$, of group order $8^{14}$. We develop its double-coset mechanism and construct counterexamples in many other groups. For $n=4$, the smallest group found has order $518\,400$, namely $A_6^2\times C_2^2$; no absolute minimality is claimed. For $n=6$ there is a witness in a group of order $1728$, for $n=10$ a class-three $3$-group of order $243$ suffices, and for $n=4$ a single class-two $2$-group of order $2^{23}$ works. We also obtain torsion-free examples. The violation ratio $R_n=|A_1\cdots A_n|^{n-1}/\prod_iN_i$ is greater than one exactly when the inequality fails; explicit four-set constructions attain $R_4\approx1.29$ in $A_8^2$, and a larger ratio of about $1.43$ is reported for $A_{10}^2$. For every $n\ge4$, the inequality holds in all direct powers of $G$ precisely when $G$ is abelian. For $n\ge2$ the optimal exponent $\theta_n$ is the infimum of $\log(\prod_iN_i)/\log|A_1\cdots A_n|$ over products of size at least two. We obtain $2\le\theta_n\le n-1.0768$, and an infinite family in $C_3*C_3$ shows $\theta_n\le n-1-\delta$ for every $\delta<5-2\log_25\approx0.3561$ and all sufficiently large $n$.
item.dc:creator: Christian Elsholtz

item.title: A complete symmetric rank-two modularity classification, obtained through a sharp uniform degree bound
item.description: arXiv:2611.12868v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We classify modular Nahm sums with a rational symmetric positive-definite two-by-two matrix and rational shifts. Up to coordinate exchange, every modular datum belongs to three explicit rational-point families, is a product of two modular rank-one sums, or is one of thirty-four exceptional triples on twelve matrices. The list consists of Zagier's rank-two examples, the Vlasenko--Zwegers additions and split products; no further data occur. The proof first bounds the joint degree of the distinguished Nahm point by four, using an initial degree bound of twenty-four and exact local exclusions at the prime 7. Explicit height and exponent bounds then give exhaustive arithmetic classifications in degrees one through four. Exact polynomial elimination determines all rational shifts, and published identities of q-series establish modularity of the survivors. The degree bound is sharp. The finite steps are accompanied by exact certificates, verification programs and independently implemented checks. Computational companion: https://github.com/johnngy44/math/releases
item.dc:creator: Cetin Hakimoglu-Brown

item.title: Brown-Gap Healing and Exact Completeness Thresholds for Leading-Unit Positive Linear Recurrences
item.description: arXiv:2611.10200v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We determine the exact completeness threshold for standard positive linear recurrence sequences whose coefficient lists consist of leading units, followed by zeros and a final positive coefficient. Using the generating function of Brown's gaps, we prove a necessary and sufficient condition for completeness, including the boundary case in which the critical gap vanishes. We further establish strict monotonicity of the unrounded threshold in the number of leading units, thereby resolving the corresponding leading-unit monotonicity conjecture.
item.dc:creator: Tony Newton

item.title: An introduction to discrete dynamics in condensed sets: orbits, periodic loci, and arithmetic examples
item.description: arXiv:2611.10438v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We formulate discrete dynamics internally in the topos Cond of condensed sets. For an endomorphism $f\colon X\to X$, we construct orbit quotients, backward histories, preimage trees, and periodic loci as objects evaluated on profinite parameter spaces. The framework recovers global-section dynamics, fully faithfully embeds compact Hausdorff systems, characterizes the invertible extension, and is compatible with inverse limits. It organizes $p$-adic congruence towers and shows, for a Cantor-type non-Archimedean Julia set, that classical periodic points can be dense although the internal periodic locus is not isomorphic to the compact condensed Julia set.
item.arxiv:journal_reference: Memorias de la Sociedad Matem\'atica Mexicana 10 (2026) 87-122
item.dc:creator: J. Rogelio P\'erez-Buend\'ia

item.title: The Fourier kernel and invariant trace formula of $\rm{GL}(3)$
item.description: arXiv:2611.11135v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Trace formula is an important method to study the Langlands program. Arthur obtains the existence of stable trace formula for connected reductive group. In this paper, we will give the explicit invariant trace formula of GL(3). For general reductive groups, Arthur gave an inductive proof of the existence of the invariant trace formula and provided explicit examples for GL(2). For GL(3), we successively compute the invariant distributions, give all the Fourier kernels for the GL(2) cases, and finally obtain the concrete invariant trace formula.
item.dc:creator: Haoyang Wang, Xinghua Cui, Zhifeng Peng

item.title: A Quarter-Power Bound for Chowla's Cosine Problem
item.description: arXiv:2611.11144v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: For every nonempty finite set $S$ of $N$ positive integers we prove $-\min_{x\in\mathbb{T}}\sum_{s\in S}\cos(2\pi sx)\gg (N/\log(2N))^{1/4}$. The proof uses a reversible phase kernel whose one-step and two-step laws are close in total variation. Comparison of rows and a height cutoff produce a partition into pieces of bounded mean. A Fourier rounding estimate then forces many additive triples to cross the partition. Two choices of phase density yield bounds in terms of negative mass and an exact conditional-pair defect, respectively. A logarithmic refinement gives a log-free bound at low triple density. At fixed positive triple density the log-free bound is a corollary of known boundary estimates. We give a separate spectral proof using an integer difference count and a theorem of Yip.
item.dc:creator: Abhishek Shankar

item.title: Phase Transitions for Random Least Common Multiples with Memory
item.description: arXiv:2611.11301v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the least common multiple of a random subset of $\{1,\ldots,n\}$ when the selection follows a correlated Bernoulli process with memory. The copying rule preserves the marginal retention probabilities and creates a genealogical forest. At fixed density, the logarithmic least common multiple exhibits a fluctuation phase transition at the memory parameter $a=1/2$. The boundary limits depend on how genealogical families are distributed among the divisibility classes carrying the leading arithmetic weight. Our proofs combine the von Mangoldt representation with a reduction to large primes. At fixed density, an exact expansion separates an innovation martingale from a memory term. An asymptotic projection onto the retained count identifies the contribution of memory. Marked point-process convergence and estimates for rare genealogical families give the boundary limits.
item.dc:creator: Shaochen Wang, Guangyu Yang, Wang Zhou

item.title: Becker's Conjecture on Compositions of Higher Degree Diagonal Forms
item.description: arXiv:2611.11750v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Becker's conjecture asserts that a rational composition of sums of $d$-th powers of size $[r,s,n]$, with $d>2$, requires $n \ge rs$. We show that this formulation fails over every characteristic-zero field in odd degree, and in every degree over a suitable finite extension of $\Q$. Over formally real fields in even degree, however, we prove that every polynomial composition satisfies $n\ge rs$.
item.dc:creator: Hua-Lin Huang, Yiming Liu, Huajun Lu, Yilun Tang

item.title: Doubly-Efficient Private Information Retrieval from Modular Forms
item.description: arXiv:2611.11859v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We present new information-theoretic protocols for $s$-server, doubly-efficient private information retrieval (PIR) in sublinear server time and one extra bit of space on the servers, for every constant $s \geq 2$. On an $n$-bit database, each of the $s$ PIR servers first builds and stores a preprocessing data structure consisting of $n+1$ bits (which is unique to each server, and after which the server may discard the original database). Then, each server answers a PIR query in time $T_s(n)$, by reading at most $T_s$ bits of its data structure and sending them to the user. In the two server setting ($s=2$), our PIR protocols achieve $T_2 = n^{0.82}$, matching the server time of the state-of-the-art schemes of Henzinger and Ragavan (EUROCRYPT 2026) while shrinking their storage from $O(n\sqrt{\log n})$ to $n+1$ bits. With $s \geq 3$ servers, our PIR protocols retain the $n+1$ bits of storage and additionally improve on the server time of all prior information-theoretic $s$-server schemes with $n^{1+o(1)}$ storage: for example, achieving $T_3 = n^{0.74}$ and $T_{10} = n^{0.61}$ (previously $n^{0.79}$ and $n^{0.75}$). Asymptotically, as the server count $s$ grows, we shrink the number of servers required to achieve a given server-work exponent from $s^{3.9}$ to $s$. Our results draw inspiration from matching-vector techniques (Efremenko, STOC 2009), which we generalize to handle degree-two computations in the exponent. Using this generalization, we build doubly-efficient PIR from the new intermediate abstraction of Fourier-sparse cone-delta functions. Then, we construct such Fourier-sparse cone-delta functions via a connection to modular forms and complex analysis: if a Fourier-sparse cone-delta function does not exist, then there exists a modular form which has too many roots, contradicting the valence formula.
item.dc:creator: Alexandra Henzinger, Seyoon Ragavan

item.title: Infinitude of integral Hitchin representations of Coxeter polygons
item.description: arXiv:2611.11930v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove that there are infinitely many Hitchin $\operatorname{SL}^\pm(3, \mathbb Z)$-representations of a Coxeter $n$-gon($n \geq 9$) group whose boundary parameters are fixed. We construct infinitely many Hitchin $\operatorname{SL}^\pm(3, \mathbb Z)$-representations of a specific Coxeter $6$-gon or $8$-gon corresponding to positive integral points of a generalized Markoff equation.
item.dc:creator: Seong Youn Kim, Sunghwan Ko

item.title: $\mathrm{RO}(G)$-graded norms for de Rham-Witt forms
item.description: arXiv:2611.12043v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We make two case studies of $\mathrm{RO}(G)$-graded homotopy in connection with $p$-adic cohomology. First, we identify the $\mathrm{RO}(\mathbf T)$-graded $\mathrm{TC}^-$ and $\mathrm{TP}$ of quasiregular semiperfectoid rings as multi-Rees algebras for the Nygaard and $\phi^\bullet(I)$-adic filtrations. We additionally compute $E^{h\mathbf T}_\bigstar$ and $E^{t\mathbf T}_\bigstar$ when $E$ is a general even $\mathbf E_\infty$-ring with $\mathbf T$-action, and compute $(\mathrm{TR}^n)^{h\mathbf T/C_{p^n}}_\bigstar$ in terms of iterated Nygaard filtrations. Next, we compute the $\mathrm{RO}(\mathbf Z_p)^\land$-graded $\mathrm{TR}$ of smooth algebras over a perfectoid base, providing a pushout of the works of Hesselholt and Angeltveit-Gerhardt along the base case $\mathbf F_p$. Using this, we extend Angeltveit's Norm map of Witt vectors to the de Rham-Witt complex, which participates in a "Witt coordinates" decomposition of the $p$-primary Adams operations.
item.dc:creator: Yuri J. F. Sulyma

item.title: A criterion for the set of subsums to be a Cantorval for a certain class of multigeometric series
item.description: arXiv:2611.12214v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The paper studies the topological structure of the set of subsums (incomplete sums) of multigeometric series of the form $\frac{k_1}{s} + \frac{k_2}{s} + \ldots + \frac{k_m}{s} + \frac{k_1}{s^2} + \frac{k_2}{s^2} + \ldots+ \frac{k_m}{s^2} + \frac{k_1}{s^3} + \frac{k_2}{s^3} +\ldots$, where $k_1, \ldots, k_m, s \in \mathbb{N}$. In terms of graph theory, necessary and sufficient conditions are established for the set of subsums of a given series not to be a finite union of closed intervals, as well as necessary and sufficient conditions for this set to contain an interval. As a consequence of these statements, a criterion for the set of subsums to be a Cantorval is obtained. An example of applying the criterion to a series whose Cantorval property was previously unknown is given. A more general object of study of topological properties is the set of numbers whose representations in a numerical system with a natural base and a redundant alphabet are subject to restrictions on the use of digits. It is for this object that the above statements are proved.
item.dc:creator: Mykola Pratsiovytyi, Yaroslav Vynnyshyn, Oleh Vynnyshyn

item.title: Cube tilings, partition counters, and the Calkin--Wilf and Kepler trees
item.description: arXiv:2611.12239v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: A tiling of the integer lattice $\mathbb{Z}^d$ by translates of the discrete cube $K_d=\{0,1\}^d$ cuts every translate $K_d+x$ into subcubes. We study the function $\ell(x)$ counting these parts. Its sum over every translate of $K_d$ equals $3^d$, for an arbitrary translation set. For lattice tilings with a triangular basis we obtain a dimension-reduction formula, and we describe every cocyclic lattice by a single normalized congruence. Along a cyclic generator, the counter of a signed bidiagonal lattice is a row of Stern's diatomic sequence; pairs of counter values realize the Calkin--Wilf tree, and complementary binary words realize the Kepler tree. For the binary lattice, the translated counter labelings of the cube carry generating face partitions, supplied by the tiling itself, which force the levels of the Kepler tree, and every nontrivial face partition has a unique lamination direction. Using finite Fourier analysis we prove that the ordered cyclic profile determines a standard cocyclic cube tiling lattice up to coordinate reflections. For lattices tiling by discrete boxes we determine exactly when the analogous statement holds.
item.dc:creator: Jaros{\l}aw Grytczuk, Andrzej P. Kisielewicz, Krzysztof Przes{\l}awski

item.title: Certified finite-precision readout for $p$-adic kernel aggregation
item.description: arXiv:2611.12254v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In non-archimedean numerical analysis, a verified $p$-adic approximation can determine an absolute value, and hence downstream probabilistic rankings and classification decisions, with mathematical exactness long before the underlying number is fully resolved. We turn this observation into rigorous finite-precision certificates for norm-based readouts of amplitude families. For a common error radius, a nonempty resolved set already fixes every exact maximizer, ties included, at the sharp integer absolute precision $v_*+1$, and conditioning on that set yields an exact total-variation identity separating unresolved $p$-adic mass from real rounding error. For aggregates of $p$-adic exponentials, we give a centered-moment certificate with an explicit remainder bound: on rational data it runs in exact rational arithmetic without individual exponential evaluations, attains its minimal bound at an active phase, and resolves every nonzero aggregate at high order; we also obtain an aggregate perturbation bound free of summand-count factors. For multiclass $p$-adic classifiers that decode by minimizing the norm of a class discriminant, we prove a necessary and sufficient certification condition and show that the sharp common precision threshold is $v^{(2)}+1$, governed by the second-largest discriminant valuation, so the winning discriminant need not itself be resolved. We apply these certificates to discrete $p$-adic path-integral actions on uniform affine chains, deriving explicit action centers and proving exact output-independence at zero effective quadratic coupling. Pseudocode and a reproducible reference implementation accompany the theory.
item.dc:creator: Su Hu, Min-Soo Kim

item.title: Real quadratic fields and finite quantum dilogarithms II: traces of quantum modular cocycles
item.description: arXiv:2611.12257v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study traces of quantum modular cocycles at fixed points of hyperbolic elements $\gamma\in\operatorname{SL}_2(\mathbb{Z})$, formulate an algebraicity conjecture for these traces, and prove it for the cocycles associated to 1-dimensional state-integrals. In addition, we analyse a finite TQFT associated with $\gamma$ and conjecture that its invariants for 3-manifolds agree with the traces of their $\mathfrak{sl}_2$ quantum modular cocycles. The finite TQFTs predict a yet-to-be-defined motive with cohomology equipped with a $\mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z}$-degree grading and a $\mathbb{Z}$-weight grading coming from a version of the Riemann hypothesis, which suggests a similar grading should exist for an extension of the Kauffman bracket skein module, for the framed $\operatorname{SL}_2(\mathbb{C})$ Floer cohomology of Abouzaid--Manolescu, and for the quantum modular cocycle. This leads to surprising additive identities among algebraic units, which we confirm for the complement of the simplest hyperbolic knot $4_1$, as well as for $S^1 \times \Sigma_g$ for a closed genus $g$ surface.
item.dc:creator: Stavros Garoufalidis, Danylo Radchenko, Campbell Wheeler

item.title: Lower intermediate dimensions of classical Denjoy minimal sets
item.description: arXiv:2611.12323v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the $\theta$-intermediate dimension of the minimal set of the classical $C^{1+\delta}$ Denjoy map, an orientation-preserving diffeomorphism of the circle not conjugate to a rigid rotation. This follows on from work of Kra and Schmeling, who showed how the box and Hausdorff dimensions may differ, depending on the Diophantine properties of the rotation number. The $\theta$-intermediate dimension interpolates between these two dimensions. We use the well-understood gap structure of the irrational rotation map to develop a covering strategy to get upper bounds on the lower $\theta$-intermediate dimension, and use results of Banaji to show that these upper bounds are sharp for $\theta$ in an interval.
item.dc:creator: Milo Edwardes

item.title: Avoiding short progressions in Euclidean Ramsey theory II
item.description:
arXiv:2611.12360v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Recently, Currier, Moore, and Yip developed a general framework for constructing colorings avoiding prescribed monochromatic arithmetic progressions in Euclidean Ramsey theory. Writing $\ell_m$ for an $m$-term arithmetic progression with unit spacing, they proved $\mathbb E^n
ot	o(\ell_3,\ell_{20})$ and $\mathbb E^n
ot	o(\ell_3,\alpha\ell_{6889})$ for every $\alpha>0$. We refine and simplify their framework, proving $\mathbb E^n
ot	o(\ell_3,\alpha\ell_{22})$ for every $\alpha>0$. We further establish $\mathbb E^n
ot	o(\ell_3,\alpha\ell_{21})$ except possibly for four values of $\alpha^2$, and $\mathbb E^n
ot	o(\ell_3,\alpha\ell_{17})$ for all but finitely many $\alpha>0$. Our approach also recovers several earlier results and avoids some technical arguments used in previous works.
item.dc:creator: Hei Chun Leung, Chi Hoi Yip

item.title: Orbits along primes in totally minimal systems
item.description: arXiv:2611.12395v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In this paper, we show that every totally minimal system admits a point whose orbit along the primes is dense. Moreover, assuming the Dickson-Hardy-Littlewood conjecture, we show that in any totally minimal distal system, the orbit along the primes of every point is dense.
item.dc:creator: Wen Huang, Song Shao, Hui Xu, Xiangdong Ye

item.title: A Totient Function Inequality
item.description: arXiv:1002.1998v5 Announce Type: replace Abstract: An unconditional inequality of the totient function is contributed to the literature. This result is associated with various problems about the distribution of prime numbers.
item.dc:creator: N. A. Carella

item.title: Estimates for the Number of Solutions of Algebraic Diophantine Equations: From the Circle Method to the Manin Conjecture
item.description: arXiv:1512.07079v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This work continues the research of the author on estimates for the number of solutions of algebraic diophantine equations by means of the circle method and develops this line in the geometric direction, towards counting integral points on log Fano varieties. It consists of two parts. Part 1 is the corrected version of the previous work. For diagonal equations $c_1x^{k_1} +...+c_sx^{k_s} = n$ with natural coefficients, upper asymptotic estimates for the number of natural solutions in the range $s \leq 2^k$, where the classical asymptotics is not applicable, are obtained by the circle method and the Hua lemma. The estimates are refined for $s = 2,3,4$ and various $k_i$; in the range $s > 2^k$ they agree with the classical ones. Part 2 develops the same line: from counting solutions of equations to counting integral points on log Fano varieties, where the circle method fails because of insuf ficient dimension. In the log case, the product in the Peyre constant diverges as a harmonic series. A method of analytic compensation is introduced that cancels the divergent term and returns the problem to the range of applicability of the standard scheme. The main result is a method for computing the Peyre log constant with guar anteed accuracy and certified intervals for the number of integral points whenever an estimate of the remainder of the asymptotics is known. The log constant is computable unconditionally, without the Manin conjecture; the conjecture is needed only to interpret it as the leading term of the asymptotics. An experimental verification for the algebraic torus and the Fermat cubic surface is presented.
item.dc:creator: Victor Volfson

item.title: Maximal Non-commuting Sets in Certain Unipotent Upper-triangular Linear Groups
item.description:
arXiv:1601.04133v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $\omega(G)$ be the maximum size of a set of pairwise non-commuting elements of a group $G$. We determine $\omega(UU_4(\mathbb{F}_q))$, where $UU_4(\mathbb{F}_q)$ is the group of $4	imes 4$ unipotent upper-triangular matrices over the finite field $\mathbb{F}_q$, in terms of a classical invariant of finite geometry: we prove that \[ \omega(UU_4(\mathbb{F}_q))=q^3-q+1+
u(q), \] where $
u(q)$ is the largest size of a partial ovoid of the symplectic generalized quadrangle $\mathrm{W}(3,q)$ disjoint from a fixed line. We show that $
u(q)=q^2$ for even $q$ and $
u(q)=\mu(q)$ for odd $q$, where $\mu(q)$ is the largest size of a partial ovoid of $\mathrm{W}(3,q)$. Consequently $\omega(UU_4(\mathbb{F}_q))=q^3+q^2-q+1$ for even $q$, while for odd $q$ we obtain $q^3+2q-1\le \omega(UU_4(\mathbb{F}_q))\le q^3+q^2-2q+2$; the upper bound rests on a self-contained proof of the inequality $\mu(q)\le q^2-q+1$. In particular $\omega(UU_4(\mathbb{F}_q))$ is not a polynomial in $q$, not even for large $q$. This corrects Theorem~$A$ of the published version of this paper, where the value $q^3+q+1+\omega(\mathcal{M})$ was claimed. We also study the non-commuting structures $\mathcal{M}$ and $\mathcal{Q}$ introduced there: we prove that $\omega(\mathcal{M})=q(q-1)$ for even $q$, that $\omega(\mathcal{Q})=\mu(q)-1$ for all $q$, and that for odd $q$ a non-commuting set in $\mathcal{Q}$ consisting of almost $m$ lines exists only for $m\le 5$. Exact values for small $q$ and a list of open problems and conjectures are included. Consequently for odd $q$ \[ \omega(UU_4(\mathbb{F}_q))=q^3-q+2+\omega(\mathcal{Q}). \]
item.arxiv:journal_reference: Acta Mathematica Hungarica, Feb. 2017, Vol. 151, Issue 1, pp. 82-116, 35 pages
item.dc:creator: C. P. Anil Kumar, S. K. Prajapati

item.title: A note on polynomial sequences modulo integers (revised version)
item.description: arXiv:1806.11359v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: For a real polynomial $P(x)$ we study the integer sequence $\lambda(P)=(\lfloor P(k) \rfloor)_{k\ge1}$ modulo integers. We show that for nonlinear $P$ the sequence $\lambda(P)$ is uniformly distributed (u.d.) in $\mathbb{Z}$ if and only if $P$ has an irrational coefficient other than the constant term. In fact, if all non-constant coefficients of a nonlinear $P$ are rational, then $\lambda(P)$ fails to be u.d.\ modulo every prime in a set of primes of positive density. We also study completeness: $P$ is complete modulo $m$ if $\lfloor P(x) \rfloor$ meets every residue class modulo $m$. For $P$ of even degree we prove that $\lambda(P)$ meets every residue class modulo every integer if and only if $P$ has an irrational non-constant coefficient. The same holds for every polynomial $P(x)=ax^n+c$ with $n\ge2$, and for every nonlinear $P$ with $P(x)-P(0)\in\mathbb{Z}[x]$. For linear $P$, both properties are characterized completely, and the two notions differ.
item.arxiv:journal_reference: M. Javaheri, A note on polynomial sequences modulo integers, J. Integer Sequences 22 (2019), Article 19.1.1
item.dc:creator: Mohammad Javaheri

item.title: $(G,\mu)$-Windows and Deformations of $(G,\mu)$-Displays
item.description: arXiv:2011.09163v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $k_0$ be a finite field of characteristic $p$, let $G$ be a smooth affine group scheme over $\mathbb{Z}_p$, and let $\mu$ be a cocharacter of $G_{W(k_0)}$ such that the set of $\mu$-weights of $\Lie G$ is a subset of $\{-1,0,1,2,\dots\}$. We prove that the groupoid of adjoint nilpotent $(G,\mu)$-displays as in \cite[Definition 1.0.1]{pappas}, \cite{lau2} and \cite[Definition 3.16]{E7} is equivalent to the groupoid of $(G,\mu)$-windows, which are the generalizations of windows as in \cite[Definition 5.1]{langer2} and \cite[Definition 3.3.1]{E7}.
item.dc:creator: Oliver Bueltel, Mohammad Hadi Hedayatzadeh

item.title: Integer factorization as subset-sum problem
item.description: arXiv:2205.10074v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This paper elaborates on a sieving technique that has first been applied in 2018 for improving bounds on deterministic integer factorization. We will generalize the sieve in order to obtain a polynomial-time reduction from integer factorization to a specific instance of the multiple-choice subset-sum problem. As an application, we will improve upon special purpose factorization algorithms for integers composed of divisors with small difference. In particular, we will refine the runtime complexity of Fermat's factorization algorithm by a large subexponential factor. Our first procedure is deterministic, rigorous, easy to implement and has negligible space complexity. Our second procedure is heuristically faster than the first, but has non-negligible space complexity.
item.dc:creator: Markus Hittmeir

item.title: Berndt-Type Integrals and Series Associated with Ramanujan and Jacobi Elliptic Functions
item.description: arXiv:2301.08211v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we evaluate in closed forms two families of infinite integrals containing hyperbolic and trigonometric functions in their integrands. We call them Berndt-type integrals since he initiated the study of similar integrals. We first establish explicit evaluations of four classes of hyperbolic sums by special values of the Gamma function, by two completely different approaches, which extend those sums considered by Ramanujan and Zucker previously. We discover the first by refining two results of Ramanujan concerning some $q$-series. For the second we compare both the Fourier series expansions and the Maclaurin series expansions of a few Jacobi elliptic functions. Next, by contour integrations we convert two families of Berndt-type integrals to the above hyperbolic sums, all of which can be evaluated in closed forms. We then discover explicit formulas for one of the two families. Throughout the paper we present many examples which enable us to formulate a conjectural explicit formula for the other family of the Berndt-type integrals at the end.
item.dc:creator: Ce Xu, Jianqiang Zhao

item.title: Automorphic line measures in the half-plane and the Grand Riemann Hypothesis
item.description: arXiv:2302.07834v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Poincare-type series, such as Selberg's, are known to produce automorphic functions, in the hyperbolic half-plane, the decompositions of which into eigenfunctions (genuine or generalized) of the automorphic Laplacian contain all modular forms of nonholomorphic type. We introduce a one-parameter family of explicit automorphic measures supported by discrete unions of congruent lines with the same property, except for one value of the real parameter, for which they miss exactly the Eisenstein series associated to non-trivial zeros of zeta, and the Hecke eigenforms the $L$-functions associated to which vanish as $\frac{1}{2}$. The Grand Riemann Hypothesis, a special case of which needs being analyzed, is disproved
item.dc:creator: Andre Unterberger

item.title: Lower order terms in the shape of cubic fields
item.description: arXiv:2409.08417v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We demonstrate equidistribution of the lattice shape of cubic fields when ordered by discriminant, giving an estimate in the Eisenstein series spectrum with a lower order main term. The analysis gives a separate discussion of the contributions of reducible and irreducible binary cubic forms, following a method of Shintani. Our work answers a question posed at the American Institute of Math by giving a precise geometric and spectral description of an evident barrier to equidistribution in the lattice shape.
item.dc:creator: Robert Hough, Eun Hye Lee

item.title: Geometry of multidimensional Farey summation algorithm and frieze patterns
item.description: arXiv:2410.13091v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper we develop a new geometric approach to subtractive continued fraction algorithms in high dimensions. We adapt a version of Farey summation to the geometric techniques proposed by F. Klein in 1895. More specifically we introduce Farey polyhedra and their sails that generalise respectively Klein polyhedra and their sails, and show similar duality properties of the Farey sail integer invariants. The construction of Farey sails is based on the multidimensional generalisation of the Farey tessellation provided by a modification of the continued fraction algorithm introduced by R. W. J. Meester. We classify Farey polyhedra in the combinatorial terms of prismatic diagrams. Prismatic diagrams extend boat polygons introduced by S. Morier-Genoud and V. Ovsienko in the two-dimensional case. As one of the applications of the new theory we get a multidimensional version of Conway-Coxeter frieze patterns. We show that multidimensional frieze patterns satisfy generalised Ptolemy relations.
item.dc:creator: Oleg Karpenkov, Matty van Son

item.title: Torsion of elliptic curves over quartic number fields with rational $j$-invariant
item.description: arXiv:2501.00400v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $E$ be an elliptic curve defined over a quartic extension $K$ of $\mathbb{Q}$ with $j(E)\in\mathbb{Q}$. We classify the possible group structures of $E(K)_{\mathrm{tors}}$, concluding that the only additional possibilities, besides those occuring over quartic fields by base change from elliptic curves over $\mathbb{Q}$, are $\mathbb{Z}/17\mathbb{Z}$ and $\mathbb{Z}/21\mathbb{Z}$.
item.dc:creator: Lucas Hamada

item.title: A Markov model for factorisation of iterated cubic polynomials
item.description: arXiv:2502.16202v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We introduce a Markov model for the factorisation of iterates of post-critically finite (PCF) cubic polynomials, extending the approach of Boston-Jones and Goksel for quadratic polynomials. Using the information encoded in the critical orbits, we study PCF cubic polynomials with combined critical orbits of lengths one, two and three. We construct groups $M_n$ and prove that their cycle data follow our Markov model. In certain cases, relations involving critical and co-critical points allow us to refine the model and the corresponding groups. We describe these groups using conditions arising from discriminants and prove that they contain, up to conjugation, the Galois groups of the iterates over number fields containing $\sqrt{-3}$. Our construction recovers the known Galois group associated with the cubic Belyi map and gives new groups for the other cases. Finally, we conjecture that the constructed groups coincide with the Galois groups outside a thin set of parameters at each fixed level, and provide computational evidence supporting this conjecture.
item.dc:creator: Javier San Mart\'in Mart\'inez

item.title: Orthogonality of non-pretentious functions to polynomials over Function Fields
item.description: arXiv:2509.12755v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove that non-pretentious multiplicative functions are orthogonal to polynomials over function fields (up to characteristic conditions).
item.dc:creator: Tal Meilin

item.title: Modular points and dimensions of Eisenstein deformation spaces
item.description: arXiv:2512.21249v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this article, we study two-dimensional Eisenstein deformation spaces, focusing on the Zariski density of modular points and the dimensions of their irreducible components. Over $\mathbb{Q}$, under explicit generic hypotheses, we prove that every irreducible component has characteristic zero and dimension $4$, and that modular points are Zariski dense. Over certain abelian totally real fields, we prove a big $R=\mathbb{T}$ theorem for the union of the high-dimensional components. As an arithmetic application, we prove the weight-one Fontaine-Mazur conjecture over $\mathbb{Q}$ for $p\geq 5$, with no hypothesis on the residual representation. In a complementary direction, we prove a local-to-global finiteness theorem for pseudo-deformation rings. Combining this with ordinary finiteness and modularity-theoretic inputs, we prove Mazur's dimension conjecture over $\mathbb{Q}$ in both the residually reducible and residually irreducible cases, and deduce Emerton's equidimensionality conjecture for the $p$-adic big Hecke algebra for every odd prime.
item.dc:creator: Xinyao Zhang

item.title: Discovering hypergeometric series with harmonic numbers via Wilf-Zeilberger seeds
item.description: arXiv:2602.08721v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: By extracting coefficients from Wilf-Zeilberger pairs with respect to auxiliary parameters, we discover many nontrivial hypergeometric series involving harmonic numbers. In particular, we obtain a rapidly convergent series for the depth-two multiple zeta value $\zeta(5,3)$, which appears to be the first result of its kind in the literature. We also investigate the Hilbert series attached to a WZ-seed and conjecture that it admits a remarkably simple form, suggesting the presence of an underlying graded-algebra structure associated with WZ-seeds.
item.dc:creator: Kam Cheong Au

item.title: Nontrivial torsion in the Tate--Shafarevich group of elliptic curves via visibility and twists
item.description: arXiv:2602.19861v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $\ell$ be an odd prime number. We study the visibility theorem for certain elliptic curves over $\mathbb{Q}$ with additive reduction at $\ell$, and deduce the existence of nontrivial $\ell$-torsion in $\mathrm{Sha}(E^D/\mathbb{Q})$ for suitable quadratic twists $E^D$. Assuming the Bunyakovsky conjecture for $D_k:=3796416000k^3+6840849600k^2-19745252280k-36525288487$, we prove that there exist infinitely many pairs of BSD twins with identical minimal discriminants and Kodaira symbols, both of which have nontrivial $3$-primary components of their Tate--Shafarevich groups. Via the theory of visibility, this provides an instance of the infinitude predicted by the Bhargava--Klagsbrun--Lemke Oliver--Shnidman conjecture, within the family of quadratic twists of an elliptic curve without a rational 3-isogeny.
item.dc:creator: Asuka Shiga

item.title: Analogue of the theta group $\Gamma_{\theta}$
item.description: arXiv:2602.22471v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we introduce higher level versions of the theta group $\Gamma_{\theta}.$ In particular, we treat level 3 and 4 versions of the theta group, $\Gamma_{\theta,3}$ and $\Gamma_{\theta,4}$ and prove that $\displaystyle F(\tau)=\eta \left(\frac{\tau-1}{3} \right) \eta\left(\frac{\tau+1}{3} \right)$ and $\displaystyle G(\tau)=\eta \left(\frac{\tau-1}{4} \right) \eta\left(\frac{\tau+1}{4} \right)$ are modular forms on $\Gamma_{\theta,3}$ and $\Gamma_{\theta,4}$ respectively. Moreover we compute their multiplier systems, $\nu_{F}$ and $\nu_{G}$.
item.dc:creator: Kazuhide Matsuda

item.title: Bogomolov property for modular Galois representations with nontrivial nebentypus
item.description: arXiv:2603.13523v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: A field in which the (logarithmic) Weil height is bounded from below by a strictly positive constant is said to have the Bogomolov property (property (B)). Given a normalized eigenform $f\in S_k(\Gamma_0(N))$ Amoroso and Terracini proved (B) for the field "cut out" by the adelic representation associated to $f$ under some assumptions on $f$, generalizing the earlier work of Habegger on elliptic curves. In this paper we extend this result to the case of normalized eigenforms with nontrivial nebentypus character. We also introduce the notion of ADZ field, inspired by earlier work of Amoroso, David and Zannier, exhibiting a class of fields in which property (B) is preserved under (arbitrary) composition.
item.dc:creator: Pietro Piras

item.title: Analogue of the theta group $\Gamma_{\theta},$ II
item.description: arXiv:2603.16109v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this series of papers, we introduce higher level versions of the theta group $\Gamma_{\theta}.$ In this paper, we treat the theta group of level $5$, $\Gamma_{\theta,5},$ and construct modular forms on $\Gamma_{\theta,5}$. Moreover we compute their multiplier systems. For this purpose, we derive transformation formula of theta function with characteristics.
item.dc:creator: Kazuhide Matsuda

item.title: Counting subalgebras of $\mathfrak{o}^n$
item.description: arXiv:2603.17286v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $\mathfrak{o}$ be a compact discrete valuation ring with residue field $\mathbb{F}_q$. We study the cotype zeta function of finite-index subalgebras of $\mathfrak{o}^n$ by adapting an approach developed by Voll for more general algebras. For each $\emptyset\neq I\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n-1\}$, we express the generating series counting subalgebras whose elementary divisor valuations, listed in decreasing order, have jumps precisely at the positions in $I$ as a finite weighted sum of $\mathfrak{o}$-adic integrals. We compute these integrals in several cases, obtaining explicit formulas for the generating series associated with every singleton set $I$ in arbitrary rank. We also obtain the cotype zeta function of unital subalgebras of $\mathfrak{o}^4$. As a by-product, we obtain a universal lower bound for the abscissa of convergence of the subalgebra zeta function of any $\mathfrak{o}$-algebra that is free of rank $n$ as an $\mathfrak{o}$-module. We also establish several results concerning the uniformity problem for the subalgebra zeta function of \(\mathfrak{o}^n\). To do so, we study two systems of polynomial equations over the residue field and apply the results to derive the number of irreducible unital subalgebras of $\mathfrak{o}^n$ of index $q^e$, for $e\leq n+3$. Finally, we use the decomposition of subalgebras into local factors to obtain the number of unital subalgebras of $\mathfrak{o}^n$ of index $q^e$ for $e\leq 9$. For each fixed $n$, these subalgebra counts are universal polynomials in $q$.
item.dc:creator: Aaron Blas Pereda, Diego Sulca

item.title: Weighted Recursions for Hurwitz Class Numbers
item.description: arXiv:2606.04508v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We establish new recursions for Hurwitz class numbers with polynomial weights. In contrast to previous recursions, our results decouple class numbers of even and odd discriminants. Our main tool is the vector-valued holomorphic projection operator applied to mock modular forms. We invoke representation theory to connect the relevant spaces of vector-valued modular forms to spaces of classical new and old forms. We thereby leverage the vanishing of spaces of vector-valued cusp forms not available in the scalar case.
item.dc:creator: Matthew Ortiz, Martin Raum, Olav K. Richter

item.title: A criterion for weighted uniform distribution along functions from a Hardy field
item.description: arXiv:2606.08040v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: A classical theorem of Boshernitzan states that if $f$ is a function which belongs to a Hardy field and which satisfies $|f(x)|\prec x^{\ell}$ for some $\ell\in \mathbb{N}$, then the sequence $(f(n))_{n\in \mathbb{N}}$ is uniformly distributed modulo 1 if and only if $\lim_{x\to\infty}\frac{|f(x)-p(x)|}{\log(x)} = \infty$ for all $p(x)\in \mathbb{Q}[x]$. We provide a new proof of this result using methods from summability theory and we extend Boshernitzan's criterion by obtaining necessary and sufficient conditions for $f$ to be uniformly distributed modulo 1 with respect to a broad class of weighted averages. As an application of our results, we show that for the function $f(x) = x^{3/2}$ and for any $(a,b)\subset [0,1]$, and all sufficiently large $N\in\mathbb{N}$, there is an $n\in [N-N^{\frac{1}{4}},N]$ such that $f(n)\mod 1\in (a,b)$.
item.dc:creator: Michael Reilly

item.title: Beyond Mock Modularity: Elliptic Corrections for Higher Dyson Ranks
item.description: arXiv:2607.13159v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: When $m = 1$, the Dyson rank generating function is a classical bridge between partition theory, Ramanujan's mock theta functions, and the theory of harmonic Maass forms and nonholomorphic Jacobi forms. The rank is a statistic on partitions, and the higher Dyson systems, for $m \geq 2$, are a natural multivariable refinement of it, combining $m$ graded rank contributions. Unlike the classical case, these higher systems are not expected to fit the mock-modular framework, which raises the question of what analytic structure governs them. We show that their root-of-unity specializations carry a hidden elliptic structure. For $m\ge2$, the primitive $(2m+1)$st-root specialization of their generating function leads to a product deformation whose associated seed satisfies a finite $q$-difference recurrence with an explicit polynomial defect. Using bilateral periodization we construct a meromorphic lift satisfying a twisted index-$m$ elliptic transformation law, with at most simple poles on a prescribed lattice orbit. The poles can be removed by subtracting an explicit multiple of an Appell--Lerch kernel and a specified translation removes the twist. The resulting holomorphic finite parts admit a finite theta decomposition. These results grew out of a human--AI collaboration, and the key new formulas were formalized and machine-verified in Lean/Mathlib by AxiomProver.
item.dc:creator: Claudia Alfes, Ken Ono, Ashvin Swaminathan

item.title: Sidon sets with $\Delta$-separated sumsets in additive number theory
item.description: arXiv:2608.07416v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The set $A$ is a $B_h$-set if every element of the sumset $hA$ has a unique representation as a sum of $h$ elements of $A$. A $B_2$-set is also called a Sidon set. A $B_{h,\Delta}$-set is a $B_h$-set $A$ whose sumset $hA$ is $\Delta$-separated, that is, $|x-x'| \geq \Delta$ for all $x,x' \in hA$ with $x\neq x'$. Upper and lower bounds are obtained for the cardinality of the largest $B_{2,\Delta}$-sets contained in $\{1,2,\ldots, n\}$, that is, sets $A \subseteq \{1,2,\ldots, n\}$ such that, if $a,b,c,d \in A$ and $\{a,b\} \neq \{c,d\}$, then $|(a+b)-(c+d)| \geq \Delta$.
item.dc:creator: Melvyn B. Nathanson

item.title: Prescribed Complex Multiplication in Reductions of Elliptic Curves
