item.description: arXiv:2608.17639v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study primes at which the reduction of an elliptic curve admits complex multiplication by an order in a prescribed imaginary quadratic field, a problem closely related to the Lang--Trotter conjecture for Frobenius fields. For certain non-CM elliptic curves $E/\mathbb{Q}$ and imaginary quadratic fields $K$, we show that either the number of primes $p\leq x$ at which $E$ has Frobenius field $K$ satisfies a logarithmic-type lower bound in $x$, or there are infinitely many supersingular primes at which the reduction of $E$ has CM by $K$. Assuming a $p$-adic approximation conjecture for singular moduli, we further obtain a quantitative lower bound in the supersingular case. Our approach extends Elkies's method for proving the infinitude of supersingular primes, combining a combinatorial argument with refined local estimates for singular moduli and Deuring's theory of complex multiplication. Finally, we use arithmetic intersection theory on modular curves to establish power-saving upper bounds for a restricted counting function.
item.dc:creator: Tian Wang

item.title: Imaginary Non-CM Fields of $2$-Power Degree
item.description: arXiv:2609.24114v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We establish a new method for the study of imaginary non-CM fields of arbitrary \(2\)-power degree and class number one. In particular, we show that for degrees greater than \(16\), dihedral fields either lie in the ray class field of one of the three imaginary quadratic fields \(\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{-2})\), \(\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{-3})\),\(\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{-19})\),\(\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{-43})\), \(\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{-67})\), whose conductor is supported only on primes dividing \(2\), with explicit upper bounds on the relevant exponents, or are Hilbert class fields of imaginary quadratic fields. We also give a complete classification of the \(161\) imaginary non-CM fields of degree \(16\) with class number one, providing explicit tables of defining polynomials, Galois groups, base fields, and conductors. These \(161\) non-CM fields, together with the six CM fields classified by Louboutin and Okazaki \cite{lou7}, complete the classification of all imaginary fields of degree \(16\) with class number one. For CM fields, the problem reduces to computing relative class numbers via analytic class number formulae, whereas for non-CM fields the absence of a totally real subfield of index \(2\) requires a different approach and leads to a richer variety of Galois groups and ramification patterns.
item.dc:creator: Farahnaz Amiri

item.title: Properness of the Cuspidal Hilbert Eigenvariety
item.description: arXiv:2610.12605v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove that for any prime $p$ and tame level $N\geq4$, the weight map from the cuspidal Hilbert eigenvariety constructed by Andreatta--Iovita--Pilloni for a totally real field $F$ to the weight space is proper in the sense of Buzzard--Calegari, under a non-vanishing hypothesis on certain Sen polynomials of Galois representations at the primes above $p$. In particular, this yields the properness of the eigenvariety away from non-positive integral Sen weights. Our approach extends the $p$-adic Hodge-theoretic argument of Diao--Liu. When $p$ has a unique prime of $F$ above it, we remove this hypothesis and obtain unconditional properness, by establishing base-change compatibility for spaces of overconvergent Hilbert modular forms and analyzing the associated spectral variety over certain closed subspaces of the weight space.
item.dc:creator: Yi Zhu (Department of Mathematical Sciences, Tsinghua University, Beijing, China)

item.title: On Waring-Goldbach problem for two squares and higher powers
item.description:
arXiv:2610.15142v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $
u_1(n)$ and $
u_2(n)$, respectively, denote the number of representations of the natural number $n$ as the following form  egin{equation*} n=p_1^2+p_2^2+p_3^4+p_4^4+p_5^4+p_6^5+p_7^8, \end{equation*} and  egin{equation*} n=p_1^2+p_2^2+p_3^3+p_4^4+p_5^5+p_6^6+p_7^8, \end{equation*} where $p_1,\dots,p_7$ are primes in both above cases. In this paper, it is proved that $
u_1(n)\gg n^{43/40}(\log n)^{-7}$ holds for every sufficiently large integer $n$ subject to $n\equiv1\pmod2$ and $n\equiv\pm1\pmod3$. Moreover, we also establish that $
u_2(n)\gg n^{43/40}(\log n)^{-7}$ holds for every sufficiently large integer $n$ subject to $n\equiv1\pmod2$. These results improve and enhance the earlier work of Andrade [1] and Wang-Tian [17], respectively.
item.dc:creator: Linji Long, Yunchao Chi, Jinjiang Li, Min Zhang

item.title: Low Lying Zeros of Dedekind Zeta Functions
item.description: arXiv:2610.16010v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $K$ be a number field of degree $n_K$, and let $h(K)$ denote the smallest absolute value of the imaginary part of a non-trivial zero of its Dedekind zeta function $\zeta_K$. In 1979, Hoffstein proved the unconditional bound $h(K)\leq 0.87+o(1)$ as $n_K\to\infty$. In a 1990 survey, Odlyzko announced the stronger bound $h(K)\leq 0.54+o(1)$ without proof. No improvement on Hoffstein's bound has since appeared with a published proof. We construct a comparison kernel from a linear combination of three identities and show that Hoffstein's original parameters give $h(K)<0.825$ for sufficiently large $n_K$. We generalise Hoffstein's method via Stechkin's trick and prove $h(K)<0.58$ for all sufficiently large $n_K$, giving the best proved estimate to date. Moreover, $\zeta_K$ has at least $c n_K$ non-trivial zeros with imaginary part in $[0,0.58]$, counted with multiplicity, for some $c>0$ and $n_K$ large enough.
item.dc:creator: Timothy S. Trudgian, Sebastian Zuniga Alterman

item.title: A recurrence in logarithmic M\"obius sums with coprimality conditions via Euler-Maclaurin
item.description: arXiv:2610.17720v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We derive a recurrence for logarithmically weighted M\"obius sums by combining M\"obius inversion with the Euler-Maclaurin summation formula. Consequently, starting from estimates of orders zero, one and two, we obtain polynomial approximations for these sums for every nonnegative integer exponent of $\log$. We then extend these estimates to sums with coprimality conditions via a convolution identity and to sums weighted by the reciprocal of the sum-of-divisors function. We also study the nonnegativity of the latter sums for every positive integer logarithmic order, establishing that they never change sign.
item.dc:creator: Sebastian Zuniga Alterman

item.title: On the dimension conjecture for global Galois deformation rings in characteristic two
item.description: arXiv:2610.21298v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $K$ be a number field, and let $S$ be a finite set of primes of $K$ containing all primes above $2$ and all archimedean primes. Let $G_{K,S}$ be the Galois group of the maximal algebraic extension of $K$ unramified outside $S$. We prove two refined lower bounds for the Krull dimension of unrestricted global Galois deformation rings of continuous absolutely irreducible representations of $G_{K,S}$ over finite fields of characteristic $2$. As applications, we construct the first counterexamples to the dimension conjecture in every dimension $n\geq 2$ over every number field with a real prime. Over every totally real number field, these constructions also yield the first examples of such universal deformation rings that fail to be complete intersections. Furthermore, we propose a modified dimension conjecture over arbitrary number fields and in every dimension.
item.dc:creator: Yufan Luo

item.title: Mixed Tate Chabauty--Kim beyond the polylog quotient
item.description: arXiv:2610.25365v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We develop an algorithmic approach to mixed Tate Chabauty--Kim theory for the full unipotent fundamental group of $\mathbb{P}^1 \smallsetminus \{0,1,\infty\}$, beyond the polylogarithmic quotient used in previous work. The key step is computing the cocycle evaluation map in the presence of a nontrivial motivic Galois action, using relations among motivic multiple zeta values. This yields explicit Kim functions involving multiple polylogarithms, as well as an algorithm for solving the $S$-unit equation whose halting is implied by certain natural conjectures. As an application, we prove new instances of Kim's Conjecture, including the first examples with $\#S = 2$.
item.dc:creator: David Corwin, Ishai Dan-Cohen, Martin L\"udtke

item.title: Explicit Serre weights for modular Galois representations of $U(2)$
item.description: arXiv:2610.37261v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $p$ be an odd prime. Let $G$ be a rank two definite unitary group as defined by Barnet-Lamb et al. in [2]. In this article, we determine explicit modular local Serre weights for mod $p$ Galois representations $\bar\rho_h$ associated to eigenforms $h$ of $G$, with arbitrary weights and small slopes. As a consequence, we also determine modular global Serre weights in certain cases. We show analogous results for certain Hilbert modular eigenforms corresponding to totally definite and indefinite quaternion algebras. In proving our results, we identify the non-singular submodules in quotients of certain symmetric power $\mathbb{F}_q[\text{M}_2(\mathbb{F}_q)]$--modules by Dickson polynomials and their twisted versions.
item.dc:creator: Abhik Ganguli, Suneel Kumar

item.title: A secondary term in the first moment of primitive cubic Dirichlet L-functions
item.description: arXiv:2611.01451v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: P. Gao and L. Zhao obtained an asymptotic formula for the smoothed first moment of primitive cubic Dirichlet \(L\)-functions over \(\Q\) with conductors coprime to \(3\), with a main term of order \(Q\) and error \(O\left(Q^{\frac{7}{8}+\eps}\right)\) under the generalized Lindel\"of hypothesis. Building on their double Dirichlet series, we assume the generalized Riemann hypothesis and separate an explicit secondary term of order \(Q^{\frac{5}{6}}\) in the same family, with error \(O\left(Q^{\frac{23}{28}+\eps}\right)\). We explicitly evaluate the secondary coefficient and prove that it is strictly negative. We also prove unconditionally that the secondary polynomial in the squarefree second moment of the natural cubic Hecke \(L\)-functions over \(\Q(\sqrt{-3})\) has degree one and strictly positive leading coefficient, which we evaluate explicitly.
item.dc:creator: Ziwei Hong

item.title: On the lower bound for the $L^1$ norm of Liouville exponential sums. I
item.description: arXiv:2611.03589v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $\lambda$ be the Liouville function. We prove Let $\lambda$ be the Liouville function. We prove \[ \mathcal{I}_{\lambda}(X)=\int_{\mathbb{T}}\left|\sum_{1\leqslant n\leqslant X}\lambda\left(n\right)\mathrm{e}\left(n\alpha\right)\right| \mathrm{d}\alpha \gg X^{\frac{1}{4}}. \] This removes the $X^\varepsilon$ loss in the previous result of Pandey and Radziwi\l\l~\cite{PandeyRadziwill2026}. In the second paper in this series, we will prove that \[ \limsup_{X \to \infty} \frac{\log \mathcal{I}_{\lambda}(X)} {\log X} \geqslant\frac{1}{3}. \]
item.dc:creator: Jiangpeng Li, Yu-Chen Sun, Hui Wang

item.title: Doubly Sequenceable Groups
item.description: arXiv:2208.14334v5 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Given a sequence ${\bf g}: g_0,\dots,g_m$ in a finite group $G$ with $g_0=1_G$, let $\bar{\bf g}:\bar g_0,\dots,\bar g_m$ be the sequence of consecutive quotients of $\bf g$, defined by $\bar g_0=1_G$ and $\bar g_i=g_{i-1}^{-1}g_i$ for $1\le i\le m$. We say that $G$ is \emph{doubly sequenceable} if there exists a sequence $\bf g$ in $G$ such that every element of $G$ appears exactly twice in each of $\bf g$ and $\bar{\bf g}$; such a sequence is \emph{cyclic} if its last term is $1_G$. We show that every group that is abelian, of odd order, sequenceable, R-sequenceable, or terraced has a cyclic double sequencing, and that a group is terraced if and only if it has a palindromic cyclic double sequencing. We show that if $H$ is a group of odd order or a sequenceable group and $K$ is an abelian group, then $H\times K$ has a cyclic double sequencing. We also show that if $H$ has a cyclic double sequencing and $K$ is an abelian group with no direct summand of order $2$, then $H\times K$ has a cyclic double sequencing, and we extend this to terraced groups $H$ and abelian groups $K$ with at most six direct summands of order $2$. Consequently, complete double Latin squares exist for every order, and the double sequencing conjecture holds for all groups of order at most $87$ except possibly $64$, and for all sufficiently large groups.
item.arxiv:journal_reference: M. Javaheri, Doubly sequenceable groups, J. Combin. Designs 32 (2024), no. 7, 371-387
item.dc:creator: Mohammad Javaheri

item.title: On the Drinfeld formal group
item.description: arXiv:2403.02555v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We identify Drinfeld's formal group on the prismatization of $\mathrm{Spf}\,\mathbb{Z}_p$ with a formal group arising from homotopy theory, given locally by the Quillen formal group of a decompleted variant of topological periodic cyclic homology. We also prove that this formal group extends to the syntomization of $\mathrm{Spf}\,\mathbb{Z}_p$, and that it admits a certain algebraization conjectured by Drinfeld.

item.title: The Maximum Number of Sets for 12 Cards is 14
item.description: arXiv:2501.12565v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We analyze a mathematical property of the popular card game SET. We present a revised geometric and computer-assisted proof that the maximum number of sets for 12 cards is 14 using finite field geometry, combinatorics, and graph theory. We present several computer algorithms for finding or approximating the maximum number of sets. We show a complete computer proof that iterates over all possible board configurations. We use this method to compute the maximum number of sets with 4 properties for a small number of cards, but it is generally too inefficient. With this method, we compute the maximum number of sets for 3 properties for all possible numbers of cards. Finally, we compare this to an existing approximation algorithm for finding maximal sets.

item.title: The Rabin cryptosystem over number fields
item.description: arXiv:2506.09569v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We extend Rabin's cryptosystem to general number fields. We show that recovery of a random plaintext from its ciphertext is as hard as the integer factorisation problem, provided the modulus in our scheme has been chosen carefully. We investigate the performance of our new cryptosystem in comparison with the classical Rabin scheme and a more recent version over the Gaussian integers.

item.title: On $q$-real and $q$-complex numbers
item.description: arXiv:2508.08440v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In arXiv:1812.00170 and arXiv:1908.04365, Morier-Genoud and Ovsienko introduced $q$-rational numbers $[x]_q$, rational functions specializing to $x$ at $q=1$, and their extension to $q$-real numbers, Laurent series agreeing with $[x]_q$ for rational $x$. It was conjectured in arXiv:2102.00891 that for every real $x>1$, $[x]_q$ has positive radius of convergence, with optimal common radius $R_*=(3-\sqrt{5})/2$, attained at the golden ratio. We prove that $[x]_q$ converges to a nonvanishing holomorphic function for every real $x>1$ and $|q|<3-2\sqrt{2}$. The proof gives an expansion of $1/[x]_q$ as a $q$-adically convergent series of rational functions, converging absolutely and locally uniformly on an explicit region. It also defines a positive analytic function for $q\in(-R_*,1)$. Using arXiv:2405.15970, we further obtain convergence for $|q|<2-\sqrt{3}$. We compute $[x]_q$ explicitly for some transcendental $x$, including ${\rm cotan}(1)$ and $e$. We also establish sharp inequalities for numerators and denominators of $q$-rationals when $|q|=1$ and determine the closure of the set of $[x]_q$ when such $q$ is not a root of unity. Next, we show that coefficientwise reduction modulo every $m\ge2$ is injective on the Cantor line (the extended real line with doubled up rationals and the Cantor set topology); for $m=2$, it identifies the Cantor line with $\mathbb P^1(\mathbb F_2((q)))$. We describe the inverse map, extend rationality results modulo every prime, characterize quadratic series over $\mathbb F_2(q)$ corresponding to quadratic irrationals, derive criteria for eventual parity of coefficients, and compute the real numbers corresponding to $1+q^n$. Finally, we propose a definition of $q$-complex number $[\tau]_q$, a meromorphic function in $\tau\in\mathbb C_+$ expressed via hypergeometric functions evaluated at modular functions of $\tau$.

item.title: A depth-zero principal-series block whose Hecke algebra has a non-trivial two-cocycle
item.description: arXiv:2510.07391v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Recently the authors have shown that every Hecke algebra associated to a type constructed by Kim and Yu is isomorphic to a Hecke algebra for a depth-zero type. An example in the literature has been suggested as a counterexample to this result. We show that the example is not a counterexample, and exhibit some of its interesting properties, e.g., we show that a principal series, depth-zero type can have a Hecke algebra with non-trivial two-cocyle, a phenomenon that many did not expect could occur.

item.title: New Obstacles to Multiple Recurrence
item.description: arXiv:2511.21680v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We show that there is a set which is not a set of multiple recurrence despite being a set of recurrence for nil-Bohr sets. This answers Huang, Shao, and Ye's "higher-order" version of Katznelson's Question on Bohr recurrence and topological recurrence in the negative. Equivalently, we construct a set $S$ so that there is a finite coloring of $\mathbb{N}$ without monochromatic three-term arithmetic progressions with common differences in $S$, but so that $S$ lacks the usual polynomial obstacles to arithmetic progressions. This represents a significant contribution to our understanding of when a restricted van der Waerden theorem or a restricted Szemer\'edi Theorem holds, an important problem in additive combinatorics and Ramsey theory.

item.title: The arithmetic de Rham stack
item.description: arXiv:2608.20203v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We define and study the arithmetic de Rham stack $X^{\operatorname{arith}}$ of a scheme $X$ over a field of characteristic $p$, and analyze its relation with related stacks such as the Hyodo--Kato stack. We show that $X^{\operatorname{arith}}$ gives a stack-theoretic approach to rigid cohomology and its coefficients, known as overconvergent isocrystals and arithmetic $D$-modules, which avoids the long-standing problem of frame-choosing in earlier approaches. We finally give some arithmetic applications of our formalism, such as a proof of Berthelot's conjecture on the preservation of overconvergent isocrystals by smooth proper pushforward.

item.title: Positivity and negativity for $h$-bases for $n$
item.description: arXiv:2610.19470v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: A set $A$ of integers is an $h$-basis for $n$ if every integer in $[0,n] = \{0,1,2,\ldots,n\}$ belongs to the sumset $hA$, that is, can be represented as the sum of exactly $h$ not necessarily distinct elements of $A$. The classical postage stamp problem asks for the largest integer $n_h(k)$ such that $[0,n_h(k)] \subseteq hA$ for some set $A$ of nonnegative integers of size $k+1$. We consider the effect of allowing negative elements. Let $n^{\flat}_h(k)$ be the largest integer such that $[0,n^{\flat}_h(k)] \subseteq hA$ for some set $A$ of integers of size $k+1$ containing at least one negative integer. For $k=2$, we have $n^{\flat}_h(2) < n_h(2)$ if $h$ is odd or $h=4$ and $n^{\flat}_h(2) = n_h(2)$ if $h$ is even and $h \neq 4$. Proofs of these comparison results were autonomously discovered and formally verified in Lean by https://aristotle.harmonic.fun/}{Aristotle}, a formal reasoning agent developed by https://www.harmonic.fun/}{Harmonic}. In this paper we give new proofs of these results.

item.title: On the Irreducibility of Locally Analytic Vectors in Certain Banach Representations of $D^\times$
item.description: arXiv:2611.04514v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We investigate the structure of locally analytic representations of $p$-adic groups, and establish a sufficient condition for the irreducibility of locally analytic vectors in certain Banach representations of $D^\times$, where $D$ is the quaternion division algebra over $\mathbb{Q}_p$. As an application, we prove that $\mathrm{JL}(\rho)^{\mathrm{an}}/\mathrm{JL}(\rho)^{1\text{-}\mathrm{alg}}$ is a topologically irreducible locally analytic representation of $D^\times$ under certain genericity conditions on $\rho$. Here $\mathrm{JL}(\rho)$ is the $\rho(-1)$-multiplicity space in the image of $\Pi(\rho)$ under Scholze's functor, and $\Pi(\rho)$ is the representation associated to $\rho$ by the $p$-adic local Langlands correspondence.

item.title: Gaps in the Most Frequent Sizes of Integer Sumsets
item.description: arXiv:2611.07303v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Nathanson observed that, for four-element sets $A$ of integers, the most frequent sizes of the iterated sumset $hA$ are separated by triangular numbers. Senger proved this and suggested an analogue for larger sets. We establish this pattern for $k$-element subsets of $\{1,\ldots,q\}$, for every fixed $k\geq3$, where $h\geq2$ is either fixed or grows slower than $q^{1/(2k-1)}$. As $q\to\infty$, almost every such set has the largest possible $h$-fold sumset, and almost every exception has one of $h-1$ explicit smaller sizes. The differences between consecutive sizes among these $h$ values are consecutive $(k-2)$-dimensional simplex numbers.
